I've written the record to `/Users/dev/terminal-bench/cwe-bench/stacking/out/reader/h3-ghsa-3fc8-2r3f-8wrg.json`. The candidate is usable, with 7 traps that fall into 5 independent groups.

The pinned commit comes before fix A. `/api/proxy` fetches whatever URL is in the request body, with no check on where it points (`src/app/api/proxy/route.ts:6-11`). So the advisory's route is completely open, not partly guarded.

**Traps:**
- **T1** (M4, advisory route): the open proxy itself. Easy for both models.
- **T2** (M8) and **T3** (M7), both in the same proxy route: a check on the first host misses redirects that `fetch` follows. A check on the resolved address misses that `fetch` resolves the name again when it connects. These are probably what B is about. T2 and T3 only show up once T1 has a check. Fixing all three at one site makes T1–T3 a single group.
- **T4** (M2, DeepSeek-type): `src/app/api/files/image/route.ts:7` fetches a client-supplied URL with no login check and uploads the result to Imgur. A solver could argue it's dead code, since nothing in `src` calls it and half the file is commented out.
- **T5** (M11, both types): chat requests can carry their own `endpoint`, which overrides the server's configured one (`agentRuntime.ts:35,63,96,111`). For some requests that value isn't verified at all (`auth/utils.ts:12-17`). The value that must keep working is the local Ollama address `127.0.0.1:11434`.
- **T6** (M1): the same custom-endpoint idea, reached through a request header on the speech-to-text, text-to-speech and image routes (`const/fetch.ts:17`).
- **T7**: the plugin gateway. The actual fetch is in an external package that isn't installed, so I couldn't read it.

**Recommended design: T1 (with T2/T3), T4 and T5.** These are three separate fix sites with different reasons a solver might dismiss them. The design includes one DeepSeek-type trap (T4) and one MiMo-type trap (T5). I left out T6 because it repeats T5 through another route, which makes it easy. I left out T7 because its fetch is outside the repo and plugins are meant to call any server.

**Fairness risks:**
- Blocking private hosts on the proxy breaks local plugin development, which uses `localhost` manifests.
- Applying that block to provider endpoints breaks local Ollama.
- Refusing all redirects breaks normal manifest and image URLs, which often redirect.

**Not verified** (listed in `unverified`):
- I couldn't run git, so I never saw the code of fix A or fix B.
- Saying A added a DNS lookup plus a private-IP check is from memory. Saying B is a redirect or private-IP-check bypass is from memory too.
- So `b_in_code_a_wrote: true` follows from the advisory's "insufficient fix" wording, not from reading the diff.
